outcome_summary: I_NEG is STILL not reached in EITHER cell, even at TSTOP=100us (a 5x extension over R04E22's own 20us). Both cells remain parked at state 3 (LOW_BUILD_NEGATIVE) at t=100us; t_neg_target FAILs in both. Direct byte-level parsing of both full 100,356-point .raw traces shows IL1 reaches its GLOBAL minimum of -2.2150912284851074A at t=2.817428674148355e-06s (~2.82us into the run, essentially the same value R04E22's own 20us-window IL1_MIN already captured), then RELAXES BACK TOWARD ZERO for the remainder of the window (IL1=-0.098A at 20us, -0.0024A at 40us, -0.0000236A at the final point t=100us) instead of continuing to build more negative. This refutes the 'naive linear extrapolation' assumption BOUNDARY.md Section 2 used to justify TSTOP=100us: the trajectory was never still linearly ramping past 20us, it had already peaked and begun relaxing back toward 0 by ~2.82us. Both swept I_NEG targets (-2.5A, -9.7125A) remain far out of reach. Both cells are confirmed numerically and physically IDENTICAL (0 of 100,356 differing rows in time or I(xmod:L1) between the two .raw files), for the same reason R04E22 found at 20us: the 3->4 rule never fires in either cell, so NEG_FRAC never enters the simulated physics. Per BOUNDARY.md Section 6's third anticipated outcome ('I_NEG still not reached even at 100us'), this is reported plainly with no further TSTOP extension attempted or recommended.

outcome_classification.reasoning: Both cells remain parked at state 3 (LOW_BUILD_NEGATIVE) at TSTOP=100us, the SAME state R04E22 found parked at TSTOP=20us. Direct full-trace .raw analysis shows this is not a not-yet-arrived linear ramp (BOUNDARY.md Section 2's own 'naive linear extrapolation' framing) but a trajectory that reaches its own most-negative point early (IL1=-2.215091A at t=2.817us, well inside the ORIGINAL 20us window) and then relaxes back toward 0 for the entire remainder of the window, however long that window is extended. Neither swept I_NEG target (-2.5A, -9.7125A) is reached. Because the 3->4 rule never fires in either cell, NEG_FRAC has zero observed effect and both cells' full 100,356-point trajectories are byte-identical in time and I(xmod:L1). The specific question this experiment (and R04E22 before it) set out to answer (does a rescaled I_NEG unblock the state-4 ZVS event) remains UNTESTED -- state 4 itself is never reached in either cell at either tested TSTOP. Per BOUNDARY.md Section 6's own explicit instruction, no further TSTOP extension is attempted or recommended without a separately-justified basis for one; a future attempt would need a circuit-level intervention or a smaller NEG_FRAC target within the trajectory's own observed ~-2.215A reach, not simply more observation time.
